701500.full: ἀπο-κυλίω (see: κυλίω), [in LXX: Gen.29:3, 8 29:10 (גָּלַל) Jdth.13:9 * ;] to roll away: Mat.28:2, Mrk.16:3, Luk.24:2.† (AS)

701501.full: 1. to hinder or prevent from a thing, τινά τινος (Xenophon Historicus); with infinitive, ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν to prevent from doing, forbid to do, μὴ ποιεῖν τι (Euripides) 2. with accusative only, to keep off, hinder , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus): —;absolute to stop the way , (Thucydides):—;impersonal, οὐδὲν ἀποκωλύει there is no hindrance , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

701503.full: 1. to kick off or away, shake off , ὕπνον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to spurn , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

701504.full: ἀπο-λαμβάνω [in LXX: Num.34:14 (לָקַח (Deu.25:5 A, Isa.5:17, 2Ma.4:46 2Mac 6:21 2Mac 8:6, 4Ma.18:23 * ;] __1. to receive from another; absol., to receive as one's due: Luk.16:25 18:30 (seel. λάβῃ) Luk.23:41, Rom.1:27, Gal.4:5, Col.3:24, 2Jn.8. __2. to receive back: Luk.6:34 15:27. __3. to take apart or aside: Mrk.7:33 (cf. use in π. of the recluses of the Serapeum; MM, see word).† (AS)

701505.full: ἀπόλαυσις, -εως, ἡ (ἀπολαύω, to take of, enjoy a thing) [in LXX: 3Ma.7:16 * ;] enjoyment: 1Ti.6:17, Heb.11:26 (for late exx., see MM, see word).† (AS)

s: to have a benefit, come finely off
701506.full: 1. to have enjoyment of a thing, to have the benefit of it, to enjoy , with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;with accusative added, ἀπολαύειν τί τινος to enjoy an advantage from some source, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. ironically, to have the benefit of , τῶν Οἰδίπου κακῶν (Euripides): —;absolute to have a benefit, come finely off , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

701508.lxx: in LXX for H2308 יָתַר, etc.
701508.full: ἀπο-λείπω [in LXX for H2308 יָתַר, etc. ;] __1. to leave, leave behind (in π. a term. techn. in wills; see MM, see word): 2Ti.4:13 4:20, Tit.1:5; pass., to be reserved, remain: Heb.4:6, 9 10:26. __2. to desert, abandon: Ju 6.† (AS)

701516.full: ἀπολογέομαι, -οῦμαι (ἀπό, λόγος), [in LXX: Jer.12:1 (רִיב) Jer.31:6, 2Ma.13:26 * ;] __1. to defend: with accusative, Rom.2:15. __2. to defend one's self: absol., Luk.21:14, Act.26:1; before ὅτι, Act.25:8; τί, to adduce something in one's defence, Luk.12:11, Act.26:24 (ταῦτα) Act.24:10 (τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ); περί, with genitive of thing(s), and ἐπί, with genitive of person(s), Act.26:2; with dative of person(s), Act.19:33, 2Co.12:19.† (AS)

701518.full: ἀπολογία, -ας, ἡ (ἀπολογέομαι), [in LXX: Wis.6:10 * ;] a speech in defence: Act.25:16, 2Co.7:11, Php.1:7, 16, 2Ti.4:16; with dative of person(s), 1Co.9:3, 1Pe.3:15; before πρός, Act.22:1.† (AS)

701520.full: ἀπο-λούω [in LXX: Job.9:30 (רָחַץ)* ;] to wash off, wash away; mid., metaphorically, with accusative of thing(s), to wash off oneself: ἀμαρτίας, Act.22:16; absol., ἀπελούσασθε, ye washed yourselves clean (cf. Cremer, 406), 1Co.6:11.† (AS)

701522.full: to release on payment of ransom , with genitive pretii, Philipp. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

s: release effected by pay­ment of ransom, redemption, deliverance
701523.full: ἀπο-λύτρωσις, -εως, ἡ (ἀπολυτρόω, to release on payment of ransom, cf. λύτρον), [in LXX: Da (LXX) Dan.4:30 with * ;] release effected by pay­ment of ransom, redemption, deliverance; metaphorically, Heb.11:35; of deliverance thr. Christ from evil and the consequences of sin: Luk.21:28, Rom.3:24 (Vau., in l) 8:23, 1Co.1:30, Eph.1:7, 14 4:30, Col.1:14, Heb.9:15. (On the extent to WH. the word retains the sense of ransom, see ICC, Rom.3:24, Westc., He., 297 ff.; see also ICC, Eph., 11; DCG, ii, 605; Cremer, 410; Deiss., LAE, 331; Lft., Notes, 271, 316; Tr., Syn., § 77.)† (AS)

701524.lxx: in LXX for שׁוּב, etc., frequently in 1-4 Mac
701524.full: ἀπο-λύω [in LXX for שׁוּב, etc., frequently in 1-4 Mac ;] __1. to set free, release: Luk.13:12, Jhn.19:10, al.; a debtor, Mat.18:27; metaphorically, of forgive­ness, Luk.6:37. __2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mat.15:23, Luk.2:29 9:12, Act.19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mat.1:19 5:31-32 19:3, 8 19:10 Mrk.10:2, 4 10:11, Luk.16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mrk.10:12. Mid., to depart: Act.28:25 (MM, see word) (AS)

701527.full: απο-μάσσω (μάσσω, Att... -ττω, to touch, handle), [in LXX: Tob.7:17 * ;] to wipe off, wire clean: mid., Luk.10:11.† (AS)

701532.full: ἀπο-νέμω (νέμω, to distribute), [in LXX: Deu.4:19 (חָלַק), 3Ma.1:7 3Mac 3:16 * ;] to assign, apportion: 1Pe.3:7. (In π. of a Prefect who renders to all their dues; see MM, see word)† (AS)

701533.lxx: in LXX for שָׁטַף, רָחַץ, מָחָה
701533.full: ἀπο-νίπτω [in LXX for שָׁטַף, רָחַץ, מָחָה ;] to wash off: mid. (reflex.), τ. χεῖρας, Mat.27:24.† (AS)

701538.full: to drive from house and home, banish , (Plutarch):—;Pass., γῆς ἀποξενοῦσθαι (Euripides) (ML)

s: to be dried up, run dry
701539.full: 1. to dry up a river, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be dried up, run dry , of rivers, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally to dry completely , τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides) (ML)

701540.full: to strip off as it were a skin, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

701542.full: to make trial, essay , or proof of a thing or person, with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;so also in Act., ἀποπειρᾶσαι τοῦ Πειραιῶς to make an attempt on the Peiraeeus, (Thucydides) (ML)

s: to start off from, turn away from
701544.full: 1. to leap off from , ἵππου (Plutarch) 2. to start off from, turn away from , τινός (Xenophon Historicus) 3. absolute to leap off, start off , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

701546.lxx: in LXX for מָלַל, נָפַל, etc.
701546.full: ἀπο-πίπτω [in LXX for מָלַל, נָפַל, etc. ;] to fall off: Act.9:18.† (AS)

701547.lxx: in LXX for נָדַח hi., נָטָה hi., שׁוּב pi.
701547.full: ἀπο-πλανάω, -ῶ [in LXX for נָדַח hi., נָטָה hi., שׁוּב pi. ;] to cause to go astray; metaphorically, of leading into error: Mrk.13:22; pass., to be led astray: 1Ti.6:10.† (AS)

701549.lxx: in LXX chiefly for כָּבַס pi.
701549.full: ἀπο-πλύνω [in LXX chiefly for כָּבַס pi. ;] to wash off: seel. for πλύνω, Luk.5:2, Rec.† (AS)

701551.full: ἀπο-πνίγω [in LXX: Nam.2:13 (חָנַק pi.), Tob.3:8 * ;] to choke: Mat.13:7, Luk.8:7; pass., of drowning (= καταποντίζομαι), Luk.8:33.† (AS)

701554.full: a sending away: getting rid of an illness, (Lucian) (ML)

s: to be at a loss, be perplexed
701559.lxx: in LXX for צָרַר, מוּךְ, etc.
701559.full: ἀπορέω, -ῶ (ἄπορος, ἀ- neg., πόρος, a way, resource), [in LXX for צָרַר, מוּךְ, etc. ;] to be at a loss, be perplexed: absol., Mrk.6:20 (ἐποίει, R, mg.); mid., be in doubt: absol., 2Co.4:8; with accusative, Act.25:20; before περί, Luk.24:4; ἐν, Gal.4:20; περὶ τίνος λέγει, Jhn.13:22.† SYN.: διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, διστάζω, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491) (AS)

701560.full: ἀπορία, -ας, ἡ (ἀπορέω), [in LXX for בֶּהָלָה, etc. ;] perplexity: Luk.21:25 (MM, see word; on the construction, see Field, Notes, 74 f.).† (AS)

701563.lxx: in LXX for שָׁלַךְ hi., etc.
701563.full: ἀπο-ρίπτω (Rec. -ρρίπτω, c1.), [in LXX for שָׁלַךְ hi., etc. ;] to throw away, cast forth: reflexively, Act.27:43 (BV, cast themselves overboard; see MM, see word).† (AS)

s: to be extinguished, go out, cease to exist
701567.full: 1. to put out, extinguish, quench , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. Pass., with future middle aorist2 and perfect active intransitive, and aor1 passive—; to be extinguished, go out, cease to exist , (Euripides) (ML)

701568.full: to shake off :—; Mid. to shake off from oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus); of a horse, to throw his rider, (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically, ἀποσείεσθαι λύπην (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

701569.full: 1. to cease speaking, maintain silence , (Isocrates Orator) 2. transitive to keep secret , (Lucian) (ML)

s: to pack and remove one's goods
701572.full: ἀπο-σκευάζω [in LXX: Lev.14:36 (פָּנָה pi.) * ;] to pack and carry off; mid., to pack and remove one's goods: Act.21:15, Rec. (see ἐπισ-).† ἐπι-σκευάζω, [in LXX for pm pi., etc. ;] to equip, make ready; mid., to make one's preparations: Act.21:15.† (AS)

701577.full: 1. to look away from other objects at one, to look steadily , πρός τινα or τι (Sophocles Tragicus); εἴς τι (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with accusative to look to, regard , (Euripides); so in Mid., (Plutarch) (ML)

701578.full: to caurse one to be far away

701580.full: to strip off the scalp in Scythian fashion : metaphorically in Pass. to be shaved bare , κρᾶτ᾽ ἀπεσκυθισμένη (Euripides) (ML)

s: to be off in a hurry
701581.full: 1. to scare away , as one does birds or flies, (Aristophanes Comicus); metaphorically, ἀποσοβῆσαι τὸν γέλων (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. intransitive to be off in a hurry , οὐκ ἀποσοβήσει; i. e. be off! (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

701582.full: that which is torn off, a piece, rag, shred , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to draw off or away, tear away
701583.lxx: in LXX for נָתַק: ni., hi., etc.
701583.full: ἀπο-σπάω, -ῶ [in LXX for נָתַק: ni., hi., etc. ;] to draw off or away, tear away (MM, see word): Act.20:30; μάχαιραν, draw a sword, Mat.26:51; pass., to be parted or withdrawn (Field, Notes, 134; but see Thayer, see word), Luk.22:41, Act.21:1.† (AS)

701584.full: 1. to let fall drop by drop, distil , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. intransitive to fall in drops, distil , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

701586.full: άποστασία, -ας, ἡ (ἀφίστημι), [in LXX for מַעַל, etc. ;] defection, apostasy, revolt; in late Gk. (MM, Exp., viii; Lft., Notes, 111; Cremer, 308) for cl. ἀπόστασις, frequently in sense of political revolt, in LXX (e.g. Jos.22:22, 2Ch.29:19, Jer.2:19) and NT always of religious apostasy: Act.21:21, 2Th.2:3.† (AS)

701587.full: ἀποστάσιον, -ου, τό (ἀφίστημι), [in LXX; Deu.24:1, 3, Jer.3:8, Isa.50:1 (כְּרִיתוּת) * ;] __1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.). __2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: Mat.19:7, Mrk.10:4; in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, see word), Mat.5:31 (for other late exx., see MM, l.with; Kennedy, Sources, 121).† (AS)

701588.full: 1. a standing away from , and so, 2. a defection, revolt , ἀπό τινος or τινος (Herdotus Historicus); πρός τινα (Thucydides) 3. departure from , βίου (Euripides) 4. distance, interval , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

701589.full: 1. to stand aloof from, depart from, be far from , with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἀπ. φίλων to fall off from one's friends, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to stand aloof or afar off , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

701592.lxx: in LXX very freq., almost always for שׁלח
701592.full: ἀπο-στέλλω, [in LXX very freq., almost always for שׁלח ;] prop., to send away, to dispatch on service; __1. to send with a commission, or on service; __(a) of persons: Christ, Mat.10:40; the apostles, 10:16; servants, Mrk.12:2; angels, 13:27; __(b) of things: ὄνος, Mat.21:3; τὸ δρέπανον, Mrk.4:29; τ. λόγον, Act.10:36; τ. ἐπαγγελίαν (i.e. the promised Holy Spirit), Luk.24:49, Rec.; before εἰς, Mat.20:2, Luk.11:49, Jhn.3:17; ὀπίσω, Luk.19:14; ἔμπροσθεν, Jhn.3:28; πρὸ προσώπου, Mat.11:10; πρός, Mat.21:34; with ref. to sender or place of departure: ἀπό, Luk.1:26 (Rec. ὑπό); παρά, Jhn.1:6; ἐκ, ib. 1:19; ὑπό, Act.10:17 (Rec. ἀπό); before inf., Mrk.3:14, al.; ἵνα, Mrk.12:2, al.; εἰς (of purpose), Heb.1:14; without direct obj.: before πρός, Jhn.5:33; λέγων, Jhn.11:3; ἀποστείλας, with indic., Mat.2:16, Act.7:14, Rev.1:1. __2. to send away, dismiss: Luk.4:18, Mrk.5:10 8:26 12:3 (cf. ἐξ-, συν-αποστέλλω). SYN.: πέμπω, the general term. ἀ. "suggests official or authoritative sending" (see Thayer, see word πέμπω; Westc., Jo., 298; Epp. Jo., 125; Cremer, 529; MM, see word). (AS)

s: to put away from one, reject
701594.full: to love no more , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;hence to put away from one, reject , Lat. abominari, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

701595.full: ἀπο-στερέω, -ῶ (στερέω, to rob), [in LXX: Exo.21:10 (גָּרַע), Deu.24:14 (עָשַׁק), Mal.3:5, Sir.4:1 29:6-7 31:21-22 * ;] to defraud, deprive of, despoil (in cl. chiefly of the misappropriation of trust funds, Field, Notes, 33; cf. MM, see word): absol., Mrk.10:19, 1Co.6:8; with accusative of person(s), 1Co.7:5. Mid., endure deprivation: 1Co.6:7 (WM, § 38, 3; but see Bl., § 54, 5; M, Pr., 162); pass., ἀπεστερημένοι, bereft of: 1Ti.6:5.† (AS)

s: In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship
701596.lxx: in LXX: Deu.22:7, 3Ki.4:34 9:16 Psa.78:49, Ecc.8:8, Sng.4:13 (for שָׁלַח and its cognates), 1Es.9:51 Est.9:54, Jer.32:36, Bar.2:25, 1Ma.2:18, 2Ma.3:2 *.
701596.full: ἀπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀποστέλλω), [in LXX: Deu.22:7, 3Ki.4:34 9:16 Psa.78:49, Ecc.8:8, Sng.4:13 (for שָׁלַח and its cognates), 1Es.9:51 Est.9:54, Jer.32:36, Bar.2:25, 1Ma.2:18, 2Ma.3:2 *.] __1. In cl., a sending away (MM, see word), as, an expedition (Hdt.). __2. In LXX __(a) discharge, dis­missal (Ecc.8:8); __(b) a gift (3Ki.9:16, 1Ma.2:13). __3. In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship: Act.1:25, Rom.1:5, 1Co.9:2, Gal.2:8 (Cremer, 530).† (AS)

s: to turn away from allegiance, pervert
701598.full: ἀπο-στρέφω [in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ;] trans., with accusative, __(a) to turn away, remove: Rom.11:26, 2Ti.4:4; metaphorically, to turn away from allegiance, pervert: Luk.23:14; __(b) to turn back, return: μάχαιραν, Mat.26:52. Pass., reflex., to turn oneself away from: with accusative, Mat.5:42, 2Ti.1:15, Tit.1:14, Heb.12:25; so act., absol., Act.3:26 (cf. Sir.8:5; Bl., § 53, 1; Cremer, 880).† (AS)

s: a turning away from, an escape from
701599.full: 1. a turning back , (Xenophon Historicus); ἀποστροφὴν λαμβάνειν to have one's course turned, (Plutarch) 2. a turning away from, an escape from a thing, with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a resort, resource , (Herdotus Historicus):—;with genitive objecti, ὕδατος ἀπ. a resource or means for getting water, (Euripides); σωτηρίας ἀπ. (Thucydides) (ML)
